standard_prerequisites.name: n-types
standard_prerequisites.statement: X is an n-type if its n-fold iterated path spaces are contractible, with the cases n = -2 (contractible) and n = -1 (mere proposition) as the base of the hierarchy.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof is an induction on n whose base case is contractibility and whose step reduces the claim to a statement about path spaces.

standard_prerequisites.name: Retractions
standard_prerequisites.statement: p : X -> Y is a retraction if it has a section s with a homotopy p o s ~ 1.
standard_prerequisites.use: The section s and the homotopy epsilon are the data used to build the retraction of path spaces at source lines 81-87.

standard_prerequisites.name: Retracts of contractible types are contractible
standard_prerequisites.statement: A retract of a contractible type is contractible.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the base case n = -2 at source line 77.

core_obligations: Induct on n, with the case n = -2 discharged by the fact that a retract of a contractible type is contractible (source lines 76-77).
In the step, assume every retract of an n-type is an n-type and let X be an (n+1)-type; fix y, y' : Y and aim to show that y = y' is an n-type (source lines 79-80).
Choose a section s of p and a homotopy epsilon : p o s ~ 1, and note that s(y) = s(y') is an n-type because X is an (n+1)-type (source lines 81-82).
Exhibit y = y' as a retract of s(y) = s(y'): the section is ap s and the retraction is t(q) := opp(epsilon_y) `ct` ap p q `ct` epsilon_{y'} (source lines 83-87).
Discharge the retraction identity by the naturality of the homotopy epsilon, which gives opp(epsilon_y) `ct` ap p (ap s r) `ct` epsilon_{y'} = r for every r : y = y' (source lines 88-91).

proof_roadmap.step: Base case n = -2 by closure of contractible types under retracts.
Induction step: reduce the claim to a statement about the path space of X, which is known to be an n-type.
Write y = y' as a retract of s(y) = s(y') with explicit section and retraction.
Verify the retraction identity using naturality of the homotopy epsilon.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.1.4 at source lines 68-73: if p : X -> Y is a retraction and X is an n-type then Y is an n-type. The author's proof (source lines 75-92) is an induction on n in which the step is a genuine construction: after fixing y, y' : Y one must exhibit the path space y = y' as a retract of s(y) = s(y') (source line 83), and this requires writing down both the section ap s and the retraction t(q) := opp(epsilon_y) `ct` ap p q `ct` epsilon_{y'} (source lines 85-87). The retraction identity is not definitional and is discharged at source line 91 by the naturality of the homotopy epsilon : p o s ~ 1, which is exactly the point where the chosen section and homotopy have to interact.
